findings.title: Dynamic imports are still started eagerly for every app
findings.body: Every value in the appStore object is the result of calling import() when this module is first evaluated, e.g. applecalendar: import("./applecalendar") on line 3 and similarly for all 29 apps. Any module that imports appStore (videoClient, payment helpers, booking handlers, etc.) therefore starts loading every app package even when it only needs one, defeating the purpose of async/lazy loading and paying the import side-effect cost up front. A rejected import for an unused app also becomes an unhandled promise rejection because nothing ever awaits that particular promise. These should be thunks, e.g. applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar"), with callers invoking the thunk so only the requested app is loaded.

findings.title: Recurring-booking calendar deletions are pushed to apiDeletes asynchronously and never awaited
findings.body: In the allRemainingBookings branch, credentials are iterated with .forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); }). The async callbacks suspend at the await, so the main flow continues past this block before any push happens; the later await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) at line 652 snapshots apiDeletes without these entries (and the pushed value is the already-awaited result, not a promise). Calendar deleteEvent calls for recurring bookings are thus fire-and-forget: the handler can send cancellation emails and return (or the serverless function can freeze) before the external calendar events are deleted, leaving zombie events, and any rejection is unhandled. Use for...of or Promise.all over map() and push the deleteEvent promises before the Promise.all.

findings.title: Async forEach makes calendar/video cancellation fire-and-forget and escapes the try/catch
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); }) is not awaited, and the surrounding try/catch (lines 124-139) cannot catch rejections from the async callback because forEach ignores the returned promises. Reschedule() proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true before the old calendar/video events are actually deleted, and a failing dynamic import or deleteEvent becomes an unhandled rejection instead of being logged. Replace with await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...)) inside the try block.

findings.title: requestReschedule does not await calendar/video deletions before emailing and returning
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); }) discards the promises returned by the async callbacks. The mutation immediately continues to sendRequestRescheduleEmail and the webhook flow and can return while getCalendar/deleteEvent/deleteMeeting are still in flight; on serverless runtimes the work may be dropped entirely, leaving the original calendar/video event in place after the booking is marked CANCELLED, and failures are unhandled rejections. Await the deletions, e.g. await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... })), before sending the email.
